title: Two Sum
story: Two garden stones add up to the magic number. Which two?
goal: Write two_sum(nums, target) returning a tuple (i, j) with i < j and nums[i] + nums[j] == target, or None if none exist.
hints: A slow way checks every pair. Can you remember earlier numbers in a dictionary instead?
For each number, ask: have I already seen target - number? Store number -> position as you go.
socratic: What partner would the current number need?
How can a dictionary answer 'have I seen it?' quickly?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the key idea in “Two Sum”?

clean.label: One pass: use a single loop (no nested loop)
